idiom_name: class implementing the repository interface over a Map, or an object literal satisfying it
implementation_notes: Structural typing lets the fake be a plain object literal that satisfies the collaborator interface, or a class with an explicit implements clause when the interface is wide; the store is a Map or a plain object, so nothing of the classic structure has to be built. No framework is needed for working behaviour - jest.mock/vi.mock replace a module globally and are the heavier seam, while mocking libraries produce expectations rather than real behaviour. Keep the fake per test, preserve the async shape of the real collaborator, and keep a contract test against the real adapter.
pitfalls: An implements clause only checks that the class can be treated as the interface - it does not change the class type, so assign the fake to a variable typed as the interface to force the check.
A module-level Map or a singleton exported from a test helper is shared between tests and leaks state.
Returning a plain value where the real repository returns a Promise makes the suite pass while the real collaborator would await - keep the return types honest.
